description:
pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:162-168 — the LogStateJson struct only deserializes 'usable' and 'retired' state entries. Logs in other states (pending, qualified, readonly, rejected) end up with usable_from_ms = None and retired_at_ms = None — i.e., they parse as 'open window' (unbounded usable).

log_window_contains() returns true for None-on-both-sides (verify.rs:846-857). So a log in 'pending' state (never been usable!) will be accepted by SctVerifier as if it had an open window. A log in 'rejected' state (the operator has been kicked off) likewise.

Chrome's log_list.json includes pending/qualified logs alongside usable ones; consumers using Chrome's list as their trust source would be silently accepting SCTs from logs Chrome hasn't validated yet.

Suggested fix: track all five states. Map them to a CtLogState enum on CtLog. Refuse to set 'usable' window on a log whose state is not 'usable' or 'retired'. Have log_window_contains() additionally check the state — only 'usable' and 'retired' (with the window check) should be trusted.

Alternative: document this clearly in the parser docstring and let callers pre-filter the JSON. Currently neither is done — Chrome-list-derived CtLogList trusts more logs than Chrome itself trusts.

Cross-reference: this is what mozilla::pkix and certificate-transparency-go both handle explicitly. Worth getting right pre-1.0.
title: Google log_list.json parser silently ignores logs in 'pending', 'qualified', 'readonly', 'rejected' states
